_comment: The header values a network launch has to agree on. Each is a decision, not a
default.
genesis_time: the instant block 1 is stamped with. It must be a real UTC time in
the near future at launch, NOT the moment someone happened to run the build.
Emission is prorated against elapsed time, so a stale genesis pays the whole gap
out in one block — a day-old file once minted 125,485 ERTH at height 2. The
container entrypoint keeps it on the join path (only DEV_INIT stamps its own),
and scripts/ceremony.sh sets the launch time. The pol_burn schedules catch up the
same way: a genesis four days old retires four days of protocol-owned liquidity
in one block.
app_version is the app version this chain reports. It does NOT move on its own:
MsgUpdateParams cannot set it and x/upgrade does not bump it, so it stays at this
value unless an upgrade handler writes ConsensusParamsKeeper.ParamsStore itself.
Leaving it fixed is the normal Cosmos choice.
Its one consumer is CometBFT's state sync check, which asks the app its version
and compares. That is a consistency check rather than version negotiation -- and
a real one: a mismatch fails every state sync at the last step of the restore.
app/version.go must equal this, and TestAppVersionMatchesChainJSON enforces it.
block_max_gas caps how much gas one block may consume. The SDK default is -1,
meaning no cap at all: a block is bounded only by its byte size, so a single
transaction can consume as much gas as it likes and the per-node minimum fee is
the only brake on it. 100M is generous for normal use — a transfer is ~80k, a
passport registration much more because it verifies a proof — while still
stopping one transaction from taking a whole block. Governance can change it.
block_max_bytes caps a block's size: 4 MiB, not CometBFT's 22 MiB default. Every
RPC `block` answer, block part and gossip buffer is sized by it, and the proposer
alone decides what fills it (ProcessProposal does not re-check a block's txs), so
it is the only bound on what a node may have to hold and serve per block. The
largest txs it must fit (computed from the proto shapes and the code constants,
networks/blocksize_test.go): a private tx of 16 actions (genesis's bundle limit)
~270 KB, ~522 KB at x/shielded's 32-action ceiling; a registration ~280 KB, ~532 KB
at that ceiling; a contract upload at wasmd's MaxWasmSize 800 KiB; IBC relays and a
gov proposal at the 1 MiB a default node's mempool admits (max_tx_bytes). A full
block's private actions at the default cap (32) are ~506 KB. Gas alone would allow ~10 MB of tx
bytes (10 gas per byte at 100M), so blocks heavy in bytes are now bounded by bytes:
4 MiB is still four of the largest admissible tx, with the 1 MiB of evidence a
block may also carry. Governance can change it (x/consensus MsgUpdateParams); a
value under ~2.1 MiB would leave a maximal tx plus maximal evidence unincludable.
app_name / binary_version are the informational strings `earthd init` puts at the
top of the file. They are pinned here rather than taken from the build because a
genesis is only useful if it is byte-identical for everyone, and ldflags bake in
the git commit — the file would otherwise change every time anyone rebuilt it.
